feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Trump's visit to Ireland for the Irish Open tees off with diplomatic controversy
entry.summary: President Trump heads to his golf club in Doonbeg while working in some Irish diplomacy.

entry.title: Ringing in the Jewish new year with a twist on a Rosh Hashanah classic
entry.summary: Pati Jinich is a renowned chef and cookbook author. She was born in Mexico to a Jewish family, and her marzipan-stuffed challah bread blends her cultures in an exciting and delicious way.

entry.title: How China tried to control the narrative on the devastating floods in Nepal and Tibet
entry.summary: Reporting over so-called "the Great Firewall," a journalist details how to report for a global audience from Beijing despite tight obstacles imposed by the government.

entry.title: She left Canada to support ISIS. Now she's back and trying to rebuild a life
entry.summary: A young Canadian mother shares her memories of being an ISIS bride, and her harrowing escape from the extremist group.

entry.title: REMEMBERING LOVED ONES KILLED IN UNITED 93 CRASH
entry.summary: On September 11, 2001 Lori Guadagno lost her brother on flight United 93. 25 years later, the crash site is a place where she feels a sense of connection that she can't find anywhere else.

entry.title: Cost of living has gone up 3.4% in the last year
entry.summary: A new report shows the cost of living in August was up 3.4% from a year ago. Investors think stubborn inflation makes it more likely that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week.

entry.title: Yemen's Houthis say they now control land that overlooks a key shipping route
entry.summary: Yemen's Houthis have overrun Saudi-backed forces to consolidate control along a Red Sea shipping strait.

entry.title: Ethics watchdogs await RFK Jr.'s financial report
entry.summary: Health Secretary RFK Jr.'s annual financial disclosure is late. When it posts, the public could learn how much he has earned from a vaccine-related lawsuit against Merck, which RFK now regulates.

entry.title: What it takes to make a new — branded — tomato
entry.summary: Why is the grocery store produce aisle filling up with branded fruits and vegetables, like honeycrisp apples and cuties oranges? We watch the effort to make one new — branded — tomato.

entry.title: The other side of 9/11: Afghans reckon with America's long shadow
entry.summary: It's been nearly 25 years since the start of the U.S- led invasion of Afghanistan. NPR returns to Kabul to see how Afghans, now back under Taliban rule, are coping with the legacy of that 20 year war.
